mainTopic: עולא's rule about an עולה given to בדק הבית and מעילה with חרמים, then the argument of רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש over which holy animals need העמדה והערכה
overview: The amud opens by finishing a challenge against עולא. He seemed to learn a rule from the פסוק of חרם, yet he also holds that by Torah law an עולה given to בדק הבית only faces a holdup by the treasurers. The גמרא answers that the rule is only from the רבנן, and the פסוק really teaches מעילה. When asked why מעילה needs a פסוק if the item is already called 'קדש קדשים', the גמרא shows from רבי ינאי and רבי that even 'most holy' offerings like חטאת and אשם needed a פסוק for מעילה, so חרמים do too. Next the גמרא examines עולא's rule directly: a ברייתא requires redeeming such an עולה, but this is explained as only rabbinic, and the ברייתא's 'two counts of מעילה' is read as 'fit for two counts.' Then the גמרא turns to the משנה about holy animals that died. רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש argue over which animals the רבנן place under 'standing and valuing', and the גמרא tests them using רבי שמעון's wording. Finally, a ברייתא supporting רבי יוחנן reads the פסוק as speaking about blemished animals, and that discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The challenge ends: only the treasurers are involved
steps.stepSummary: This is the last word of a challenge against עולא: by Torah law, all that is involved is the role of the treasurers, the גזברין.
steps.simpleTranslation: [Yet עולא says there is nothing here except] the treasurers alone!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a challenge that began just before this piece. It points out that עולא himself said only the treasurers (גזברין) are involved, so he does not seem to require a payment by Torah law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before this, עולא used a פסוק to teach a rule about an altar-animal that was also dedicated elsewhere. But in another statement, עולא says that by Torah law the only issue is the treasurers' role, with no payment of the animal's value. These two statements seem to clash, and the next step resolves the clash.

keyTerms.meaning: The treasurers of the בית המקדש who manage money and property dedicated to בדק הבית
Only, alone

steps.confusionAlert: This line is not a new statement. It is the very end of a question that started earlier, so read it as part of that challenge.

phrases.english: The treasurers alone!
phrases.notes: This finishes a quote of עולא from just before: by Torah law, only the treasurers are involved here.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends a challenge begun before this piece
steps.kashyaTarget: עולא's use of the פסוק as a Torah-level source
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: עולא elsewhere holds that by Torah law there is only the role of the treasurers, which contradicts deriving a stronger Torah rule from the פסוק.

steps.title: The rule is rabbinic, and the verse teaches about misuse
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the rule really comes from the רבנן, and the פסוק is actually coming to teach מעילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really, it is from the רבנן, and the פסוק comes to teach about מעילה (misusing holy property).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the contradiction in עולא. The rule he mentioned is from the רבנן, so it does not clash with his view that by Torah law only the treasurers are involved.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By saying the rule is rabbinic, the גמרא lets both of עולא's statements stand. That raises a question: what is the פסוק for? The answer is that it teaches a different law, מעילה, while the rabbinic rule only leans on it as support.

keyTerms.meaning: Really, actually: the גמרא is about to explain how things truly are
The Sages; here it means 'it is a rabbinic rule'
Misusing or benefiting from הקדש (holy property), which brings a קרבן and a payment
A פסוק, verse

steps.whyThisMatters: This move separates a rabbinic rule from what the פסוק actually teaches, which sets up the rest of this discussion about מעילה.

phrases.english: Actually, it is from the Sages,
and the verse comes for misuse.
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets is added in the corrected wording; the meaning is the same.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 1
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reassigns the rule to rabbinic law and gives the פסוק a different purpose
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought עולא learned the rule from the פסוק as Torah law
steps.terutzMaskana: The rule is rabbinic; the פסוק teaches מעילה

steps.title: Why is a verse needed for misuse?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why a פסוק would be needed to teach מעילה, since the פסוק already calls the item 'קדש קדשים'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why do we need a פסוק for מעילה? It already says 'קדש קדשים' about it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer from step 2. If the item is already called 'קדש קדשים', then מעילה should apply anyway, so there is no need for a special פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The assumption behind the question is that anything called 'קדש קדשים' is plainly holy, and מעילה applies to holy things. If so, the פסוק adds nothing about מעילה, and the answer in step 2 seems weak.

keyTerms.meaning: Most holy items; here, the phrase 'קדש קדשים הוא לה׳' in the פסוק of חרם
Why does he need it? A way of asking that something seems unnecessary

phrases.english: For misuse, why does one need a verse?
"Most holy" is written about it!
phrases.notes: This refers to ויקרא 27:28, which says that every חרם is 'קדש קדשים הוא לה׳'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in step 2
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the פסוק comes to teach מעילה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The words 'קדש קדשים' already make the item holy, so מעילה would apply without a special teaching.

steps.title: Counter-question from Rabbi Yannai: the Torah spells out misuse only for a burnt offering
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back. According to רבי ינאי, the Torah spells out מעילה explicitly only for an עולה, which belongs entirely to ה׳. For חטאת and אשם, it is learned only from a teaching of רבי.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to your reasoning, what about רבי ינאי's statement: מעילה is written explicitly in the Torah only for an עולה, as it says 'If a person commits מעילה and sins by mistake with the holy things of ה׳', meaning things that belong only to ה׳. But for חטאת and אשם, we know it only from רבי's teaching.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 3 with a counter-question. It brings רבי ינאי to show that being holy does not automatically make מעילה obvious from the Torah.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ינאי reads 'קדשי ה׳' as covering only things that belong entirely to ה׳, like an עולה. A חטאת or אשם, which the כהנים partly eat, needs a separate source, the teaching of רבי. So the questioner's idea that 'holy means מעילה automatically' does not hold up. The גמרא finishes drawing out this point in steps 5 through 7.

keyTerms.meaning: And according to your reasoning: turning the questioner's own logic back against him
Spelled out explicitly
A burnt offering, burned entirely on the מזבח
Sin offering and guilt offering, which the כהנים partly eat
It comes out, it is derived

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבי ינאי is saying מעילה does not apply to חטאת and אשם. It does apply; he is only saying that the source for it is not the plain words of this פסוק.
steps.whatToRemember: The phrase 'קדשי ה׳' only plainly covers things that belong entirely to ה׳. Holy items that go partly to people need a separate source for מעילה.

phrases.english: And according to your reasoning,
that which Rabbi Yannai said:
Misuse is not written explicitly in the Torah
except for a burnt offering alone,
as it is stated: "If a person commits a trespass,
and sins by mistake, in the holy things of the Lord,"
meaning those set aside exclusively for the Lord.
But a sin offering and a guilt offering
are derived only from the teaching of Rabbi.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the assumption behind the question in step 3 with a counter-question
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The assumption that calling something holy makes מעילה automatically clear from the Torah
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבי ינאי shows that the Torah spells out מעילה only for things belonging entirely to ה׳; other holy items, like חטאת and אשם, need a separate source.

steps.title: רבי's teaching that includes lesser offerings in מעילה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא of רבי: 'כל חלב לה׳' includes the altar portions of קדשים קלים in the laws of מעילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: רבי says, 'All the fat is to ה׳.' This comes to include the altar portions of lighter-holiness offerings in the laws of מעילה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the actual source for what Step 4 said, that חטאת and אשם are learned only from a teaching of רבי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי reads the word 'כל' as adding the altar portions of קדשים קלים, such as a שלמים, to מעילה. If even the lighter offerings are included, then חטאת and אשם, which are holier, are surely included too. So their מעילה really comes from this פסוק and is not written out on its own.

keyTerms.meaning: To include; the פסוק adds something extra
The parts of an offering that are burned on the מזבח
Offerings of lighter holiness, such as a שלמים
Misusing something holy for personal benefit, which needs a קרבן and payment

phrases.english: As it is taught in a ברייתא: Rabbi says:
"All the fat is to the Lord"
to include the altar portions of lighter-holiness offerings in the laws of misuse.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source for the teaching of רבי mentioned in Step 4.
steps.raayaObject: That חטאת and אשם get מעילה only through a derivation, not from an explicit פסוק
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of רבי on 'כל חלב לה׳'

steps.title: Even 'most holy' items still need a פסוק
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reasons: if 'קדשי קדשים' alone were enough, no פסוק would be needed for חטאת and אשם. Since one was needed, the label alone does not teach מעילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why would a פסוק be needed? 'Most holy' is already written about them! Rather, it must be that even though 'most holy' is written about them, a פסוק is still needed to include them in מעילה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws a lesson from רבי's teaching. Being called 'most holy' does not, by itself, bring in the laws of מעילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חטאת and אשם are called קדשי קדשים, yet we needed רבי's פסוק to put them under מעילה. That shows the title 'most holy' is not enough on its own. This directly weakens the question from Step 3.

keyTerms.meaning: Most holy; the highest level of holiness for offerings
Why do I need a פסוק? Used when something seems already known
Even though

phrases.english: Why do I need a verse?
"Most holy" is written about them!
phrases.notes: 'Them' means חטאת and אשם, which are included all the more so once the lighter offerings are.

phrases.english: Rather, even though
"most holy" is written about them,
a verse is needed to include them in the laws of misuse.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמָה לִי קְרָא? ״קׇדְשֵׁי קָדָשִׁים״ כְּתִיב בְּהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the logical lesson from רבי's teaching quoted in Step 5.
steps.raayaObject: The label קדשי קדשים does not on its own bring the laws of מעילה
steps.raayaSupportSource: The fact that רבי needed a פסוק for offerings already called קדשי קדשים

steps.title: The same applies to חרמים
steps.stepSummary: Just like חטאת and אשם, חרמים are called 'most holy' but still need a פסוק to include them in מעילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: חרמים too: even though 'most holy' is written about them, a פסוק is needed to include them in מעילה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא applies the lesson to חרמים and so answers the question from Step 3.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 3 asked why a פסוק is needed for מעילה with חרמים, since they are already called קדש קדשים. The answer is that this label never teaches מעילה by itself, as we saw with חטאת and אשם. So the פסוק is needed, and Step 2's answer stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Items someone declared as חרם, given over to the כהנים or the בית המקדש
Also, too

steps.whatToRemember: Being called 'קדש קדשים' does not automatically bring the laws of מעילה. A פסוק is still needed, for חטאת and אשם and for חרמים alike.

phrases.english: Dedications too,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב דְּ״קׇדְשֵׁי קָדָשִׁים״ כְּתִיב בְּהוּ,
phrases.english: even though "most holy" is written about them,
a verse is needed to include them in the laws of misuse.

steps.triggerLanguage: חֲרָמִים נָמֵי, אַף עַל גַּב דְּ״קׇדְשֵׁי קָדָשִׁים״ כְּתִיב בְּהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the inference of Step 6 to חרמים, closing the challenge raised in Step 3.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The פסוק about מעילה for חרמים is needed, because the title 'קדש קדשים' alone would not teach it.

steps.title: Back to עולא's rule about an עולה given to בדק הבית
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to עולא's statement: one who consecrates an עולה for בדק הבית only faces a holdup from the treasurers.
steps.simpleTranslation: The matter itself: one who consecrates an עולה for the upkeep of the בית המקדש, all it has is a holdup by the treasurers.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to examine עולא's statement directly. This sets up the challenge that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An עולה already belongs fully to ה׳, so a second gift to בדק הבית does not really take hold on it. All that remains is that the treasurers have some claim, which slows things down. By Torah law, no real redemption is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The matter itself': going back to look closely at a statement quoted earlier
The fund for upkeep and repair of the בית המקדש
A holdup caused by the treasurers' claim
An offering burned completely on the מזבח

phrases.english: The matter itself:
One who consecrates a burnt offering for the upkeep of the Temple

phrases.aramaic: — אֵין בָּהּ אֶלָּא עִיכּוּב גִּיזְבָּרִין בִּלְבַד.
phrases.english: it has nothing but the holdup of the treasurers alone.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the חרמים discussion and returns to עולא's statement for direct analysis.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An עולה consecrated for בדק הבית is only held up by the treasurers' claim; it is not truly holy for בדק הבית.

steps.title: A ברייתא says the עולה must be redeemed first
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules that one may not slaughter such an עולה until it is redeemed, which suggests the בדק הבית holiness really took hold.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged: one who consecrates an עולה for בדק הבית may not slaughter it until it is redeemed!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges עולא with a ברייתא that seems to require a real redemption.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the animal only faces a treasurers' holdup, why would it need to be redeemed? Requiring redemption makes it sound like a real בדק הבית holiness is on the animal, against עולא.

keyTerms.meaning: That it be redeemed, bought back from הקדש with money
To slaughter it

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
One who consecrates a burnt offering for the upkeep of the Temple
it is forbidden to slaughter it until it is redeemed!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks עולא's statement from Step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: עולא's rule that there is only a treasurers' holdup
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A required redemption implies real בדק הבית holiness, not just a holdup.

steps.title: The redemption is only a rabbinic requirement
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא's demand for redemption is only מדרבנן; by Torah law עולא is right.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is only by rabbinic law.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends עולא by saying the ברייתא is speaking about a rule of the חכמים, not Torah law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מדאורייתא, only the treasurers' holdup exists, just as עולא said. The חכמים added a requirement to redeem the animal before slaughtering it. So the ברייתא and עולא do not really disagree.

keyTerms.meaning: By rabbinic law, a rule added by the חכמים
By Torah law (implied here as the opposite)

phrases.english: By rabbinic law.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting levels of law: Torah law versus rabbinic law
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא requires redemption because real בדק הבית holiness is on the animal.
steps.terutzMaskana: The redemption is only מדרבנן; by Torah law there is only the treasurers' holdup.

steps.title: Proof from the end of the ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא supports its answer: the ברייתא's last clause says that if he slaughtered it anyway, what he did is done, so the redemption rule can only be rabbinic.
steps.simpleTranslation: This also makes sense, because the end of the ברייתא teaches: if he went ahead and slaughtered it, what he did is done.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings support for its answer from the same ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If redemption were required by Torah law, slaughtering without it should not work. Since the ברייתא says 'what he did is done,' the redemption must have been only a rabbinic rule. That fits עולא exactly.

keyTerms.meaning: So too it stands to reason; the גמרא adds logical support
The last clause of a משנה or ברייתא
What he did is done; the act counts after the fact

steps.whatToRemember: An עולה consecrated for בדק הבית needs redemption only מדרבנן. By Torah law there is only a treasurers' holdup, so if it was slaughtered without redemption, the act stands.
steps.confusionAlert: 'אסור לשוחטה' does not mean slaughtering it is invalid. It is a rabbinic 'don't do this at the start,' and after the fact it counts.

phrases.english: So too it stands to reason,
since the latter clause teaches:
If he went ahead and slaughtered it
what he did is done.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer of Step 10 using the end of the ברייתא quoted in Step 9.
steps.raayaObject: That the redemption rule is only מדרבנן
steps.raayaSupportSource: The סיפא of the same ברייתא: 'אם עבר ושחטה מה שעשה עשוי'

steps.title: If it is only rabbinic, why two counts of misuse?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the claim that the ברייתא is only rabbinic, because the ברייתא's last clause says one commits two counts of מעילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, what, is it only rabbinic? If so, look at the end of the ברייתא: one commits two counts of misuse. But if the בדק הבית holiness is only rabbinic, why would there be two counts of misuse?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks its own answer from step 10, which said the ברייתא's rule is only מדרבנן. It points to the ברייתא's last clause, which seems to treat the בדק הבית holiness as real Torah holiness.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מעילה (misusing holy property) is a Torah-level sin. If someone is guilty of two counts, the animal must carry two real holinesses: one for the מזבח and one for בדק הבית. A holiness that exists only מדרבנן should not create a second Torah-level count.

keyTerms.meaning: By rabbinic law, not Torah law
The last clause of a משנה or ברייתא
The sin of using or benefiting from הקדש (holy property)
If so, used to bring up a problem with what was just said

phrases.english: Rather, what? Is it only rabbinic?
If so, say the last clause:
and one commits two counts of misuse,
phrases.notes: One count is for the holiness of the מזבח and one is for the holiness of בדק הבית.

phrases.english: but if it is rabbinic, why two counts of misuse?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the 'rabbinic' answer that steps 10 and 11 had just supported.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the ברייתא's בדק הבית holiness is only מדרבנן
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Two counts of מעילה means two Torah-level holinesses, so the בדק הבית holiness must be Torah-level.

steps.title: The ברייתא means the animal is fit for two counts
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rereads the clause: the ברייתא does not say one actually commits two counts, only that the animal is fit for two counts.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what the ברייתא is saying: the animal is fit to be the subject of two counts of misuse.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by reading the words of the ברייתא more carefully. 'Two counts' describes what the animal could be liable for, not an actual Torah-level liability right now.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under this reading, the clause no longer proves that the בדק הבית holiness took hold by Torah law. It describes a potential: in a case where such holiness truly applies, two counts would follow. So the answer from step 10, that the redemption rule is only rabbinic, still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it means, used to reread a source's words
Fit or suitable for something, though not necessarily so in practice

steps.whatToRemember: עולא's rule survives: by Torah law, giving an עולה to בדק הבית only creates a holdup from the treasurers. The ברייתא's stricter wording is either rabbinic or describes what the animal is 'fit' for.

phrases.english: This is what it is saying:
and it is fit for one to misuse it on two counts of misuse.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the wording of the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא says one actually commits two Torah-level counts of מעילה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא only says the animal is fit for two counts, so it does not prove the בדק הבית holiness is Torah-level.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה: if they died, they are buried
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא turns to a new line in the משנה about holy animals that died: they must be buried.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: and if they died, they must be buried, and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic by quoting the next line of the משנה. This sets up the argument between רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The line deals with holy animals that died before they were redeemed. They cannot be redeemed anymore and must be buried. The next steps ask which kinds of holy animals this rule covers according to the רבנן.

keyTerms.meaning: They must be buried, and no one may get any benefit from them
Short for 'וכולי', meaning 'etc.': the rest of the quote is assumed

phrases.english: And if they died, they must be buried, etc.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the עולא discussion behind and begins a new section of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Holy animals that died must be buried rather than redeemed.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: both kinds of holy animals need standing and valuing
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says that according to the רבנן, both altar animals and בדק הבית animals fall under the rule of העמדה והערכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: according to the רבנן, both animals made holy for the מזבח and animals made holy for בדק הבית were included in the rule of standing and valuing.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן explains the רבנן's view in the משנה. Every kind of holy animal needs to be stood before the כהן and valued before it can be redeemed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah says a holy animal is stood before the כהן and he values it (ויקרא 27:11-12). If every holy animal needs this, then a dead animal cannot be redeemed, because it cannot be stood up. That explains why the רבנן say dead holy animals of both kinds are buried.

keyTerms.meaning: Standing the animal up before the כהן
The כהן setting the animal's value for redemption
Animals made holy to be brought on the מזבח
Things made holy for their value, to pay for upkeep of the בית המקדש

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan says: according to the Rabbis,
both animals consecrated for the altar
and animals consecrated for Temple maintenance
were included in the rule of standing and valuation.
phrases.notes: ויקרא 27:11-12. The animal is stood before the כהן, and he sets its value.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the רבנן's position in the משנה line quoted in step 14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to the רבנן, both מזבח animals and בדק הבית animals need העמדה והערכה.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: only בדק הבית animals need standing and valuing
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש disagrees: according to the רבנן, only בדק הבית animals fall under העמדה והערכה, while altar animals do not.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: according to the רבנן, animals made holy for בדק הבית were included in the rule of standing and valuing. Animals made holy for the מזבח were not included in that rule.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש gives a different reading of the רבנן's view. He limits the rule of standing and valuing to בדק הבית animals only.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In ריש לקיש's view, the פסוק about standing and valuing speaks only about בדק הבית animals. Altar animals are left out of that rule entirely. This is a direct split from רבי יוחנן, who includes both kinds.

keyTerms.meaning: Included in, covered by a rule
According to the view of the Sages
Were not included, so the rule does not apply to them

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן says both altar animals and בדק הבית animals need standing and valuing. ריש לקיש says only בדק הבית animals do.
steps.confusionAlert: Both opinions are explaining the רבנן of the משנה, not רבי שמעון. The argument is about how far the רבנן's rule reaches.

phrases.english: And Reish Lakish says: according to the Rabbis,

phrases.aramaic: קׇדְשֵׁי בֶּדֶק הַבַּיִת הָיוּ בִּכְלַל הַעֲמָדָה וְהַעֲרָכָה,
phrases.english: animals consecrated for Temple maintenance were included in the rule of standing and valuation,

phrases.aramaic: קׇדְשֵׁי מִזְבֵּחַ לֹא הָיוּ בִּכְלַל הַעֲמָדָה וְהַעֲרָכָה.
phrases.english: but animals consecrated for the altar were not included in the rule of standing and valuation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an opposing reading of the רבנן to the one רבי יוחנן gave in step 15.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to the רבנן, only בדק הבית animals need העמדה והערכה; altar animals are not included.

steps.title: What Both Sides Agree On
steps.stepSummary: Both רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש agree that according to רבי שמעון, בדק הבית animals are not under העמדה והערכה, while altar animals are. Everyone also agrees that an animal blemished from the start is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Both רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש agree about רבי שמעון's view: animals given to בדק הבית were not included in the rule of 'standing and valuing,' and animals given to the altar were included. And everyone agrees that an animal that was blemished from the very beginning was not included in that rule.
steps.whatsHappening: After showing where רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש argue, the גמרא lists the points they both agree on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Their argument is only about the opinion of the רבנן. For רבי שמעון, both say that only altar animals fall under העמדה והערכה, so a dead בדק הבית animal can still be redeemed. Separately, an animal that was already blemished when it was consecrated was never under העמדה והערכה according to anyone.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Standing and valuing': the animal must be stood before a כהן and valued before it can be redeemed. A dead animal cannot be stood up, so it cannot be redeemed.
Things consecrated for the upkeep of the בית המקדש, which are worth money but are not brought as offerings.
Animals consecrated to be brought as offerings on the altar.
An animal that was already blemished before it was consecrated.
Everyone agrees.

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two arguments. רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש argue about what the רבנן hold. On what רבי שמעון holds, they agree.

phrases.english: And both this one and that one agree regarding Rabbi Shimon,
phrases.notes: 'This one and that one' means רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש from the last two steps.

phrases.english: that animals consecrated for Temple maintenance
were not included in the rule of standing and valuation,
and animals consecrated for the altar
were included in the rule of standing and valuation,
and everyone agrees
that an animal blemished from the outset
was not included in the rule of standing and valuation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the argument of steps 15 and 16 by listing the points both sides agree on.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי שמעון, only altar animals are under העמדה והערכה. Everyone agrees that an animal blemished from the start is not.

steps.title: רבי שמעון's Wording Fits רבי יוחנן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי שמעון from the משנה and shows that his specific wording makes sense according to רבי יוחנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in the משנה that רבי שמעון says: 'Animals of בדק הבית that died may be redeemed.' This fits רבי יוחנן, who said that according to the רבנן both kinds of animals were under העמדה והערכה. That is why רבי שמעון had to spell out that he means animals of בדק הבית.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a challenge against ריש לקיש. First it shows that רבי שמעון's wording works well according to רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי יוחנן, the רבנן said both kinds of animals must be buried. So רבי שמעון had to say 'קדשי בדק הבית' to make clear that he disagrees only about those, and not about altar animals. The next step will ask why he would need this wording according to ריש לקיש.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Granted': this fits well for one view. It usually leads into a question on another view.
They may be redeemed.
'That is why it was necessary': it explains why certain words were needed.
To spell out or specify.

phrases.english: We learned in the Mishna: Rabbi Shimon says:
'Animals consecrated for Temple maintenance that died may be redeemed.'
Granted, according to Rabbi Yochanan, who said that according to the Rabbis
both this and that
phrases.notes: He means both altar animals and בדק הבית animals.

phrases.english: were included in the rule of standing and valuation,
that is why Rabbi Shimon needed to specify
'animals consecrated for Temple maintenance that died may be redeemed.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the wording of the משנה to test the two explanations from steps 15 and 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's reading of the רבנן (step 16).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי שמעון's specific wording is needed only according to רבי יוחנן. This sets up the question of why it would be needed according to ריש לקיש.

steps.title: Why Specify According to ריש לקיש?
steps.stepSummary: According to ריש לקיש, the רבנן were only talking about בדק הבית animals anyway. So רבי שמעון could have simply said 'if they died, they may be redeemed.'
steps.simpleTranslation: But according to ריש לקיש, why did רבי שמעון need to spell it out? He should just have said, 'If they died, they may be redeemed!'
steps.whatsHappening: This is the actual challenge against ריש לקיש: the extra words in רבי שמעון's statement seem unnecessary according to him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the רבנן only meant בדק הבית animals, then any disagreement from רבי שמעון would obviously be about those same animals. Naming 'קדשי בדק הבית' would add nothing. The extra words seem to show that the רבנן were talking about altar animals too, which is רבי יוחנן's view.

keyTerms.meaning: 'But': here it brings the question against the second view.
'Let him say': he should have said it this simpler way.
If they died.

phrases.english: But according to Reish Lakish,
why did he need to specify?
Let him say: 'If they died they may be redeemed'!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לְרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ, לְמָה לֵיהּ לְפָרוֹשֵׁי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the challenge that step 18 set up with בשלמא.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's claim that the רבנן were only talking about בדק הבית animals.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If ריש לקיש is right, the words 'קדשי בדק הבית' in רבי שמעון's statement are unnecessary.

steps.title: רבי שמעון Covered Both Possibilities
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש answers that רבי שמעון did not know which animals the תנא קמא meant. So he answered both ways: he agrees about altar animals, but holds that בדק הבית animals can be redeemed.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש can answer you: רבי שמעון did not know what the תנא קמא meant. So this is what he said to him: 'If you mean altar animals, I agree with you. If you mean בדק הבית animals, then if they died, they may be redeemed.'
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש defends his view by explaining that רבי שמעון's extra wording comes from his doubt about what the first opinion meant.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The extra words do not prove what the רבנן actually held. They only show that רבי שמעון was covering both possible readings. So ריש לקיש can still say the רבנן meant only בדק הבית animals.

keyTerms.meaning: The first, unnamed opinion in the משנה (here, the רבנן).
He did not know (he was unsure).
I agree with you.

steps.whatToRemember: רבי שמעון's words 'קדשי בדק הבית' fit רבי יוחנן easily. ריש לקיש explains them as רבי שמעון answering both possible meanings of the תנא קמא, so his view still stands.

phrases.english: Reish Lakish could say to you:
Rabbi Shimon did not know
what the first tanna meant,
phrases.notes: He wasn't sure whether 'they must be buried' was about altar animals or בדק הבית animals.

phrases.english: and this is what he said to him:
If you mean animals consecrated for the altar, I agree with you;

phrases.aramaic: בְּקׇדְשֵׁי בֶּדֶק הַבַּיִת — אִם מֵתוּ יִפָּדוּ.
phrases.english: if animals consecrated for Temple maintenance, if they died they may be redeemed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 19.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterprets the speaker's intent: the wording reflects רבי שמעון's doubt, not what the תנא קמא actually held.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי שמעון's specific wording shows that the רבנן meant both kinds of animals.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי שמעון was answering both possible meanings, so the wording proves nothing against ריש לקיש.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports רבי יוחנן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא that reads the פסוק about setting an animal before the כהן as talking about blemished animals that get redeemed.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא was taught that agrees with רבי יוחנן: "If it is an animal of which they may bring an offering": the verse is speaking about blemished animals, that they may be redeemed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא as support for רבי יוחנן. The ברייתא says the פסוק about standing and valuation is talking about blemished animals being redeemed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן held that, according to the רבנן, altar animals that became blemished also need העמדה והערכה. The פסוק of standing and valuation speaks of an animal 'that may not be offered,' and this ברייתא reads that as a blemished animal (one that was holy for the מזבח) being redeemed. That fits רבי יוחנן and works against ריש לקיש, who limited העמדה והערכה to בדק הבית animals.

keyTerms.meaning: Blemished animals, which are not fit to be brought on the altar
That they may be redeemed
The verse is speaking about this case
Standing the animal before the כהן and having it valued, as part of redeeming it

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the first outside source the גמרא brings into the רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש argument, and it leans toward רבי יוחנן.

phrases.english: It was taught in a ברייתא in line with רבי יוחנן:
"If it be an animal of which they may [not] bring an offering"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 27:11. The full פסוק says 'any non-kosher animal of which they may not bring an offering'; the ברייתא just quotes part of it.

phrases.english: about blemished animals, that they may be redeemed
the verse is speaking.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the back-and-forth over רבי שמעון's wording, the גמרא brings outside support for רבי יוחנן's side of the argument.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's view that according to the רבנן, blemished altar animals are redeemed through העמדה והערכה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא reading the פסוק in ויקרא פרק כז as speaking about blemished animals being redeemed.

steps.title: Maybe the verse means a non-kosher animal
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks whether the פסוק might really be about a non-kosher animal instead of a blemished one.
steps.simpleTranslation: You say it is about blemished animals. Or maybe it is only about a non-kosher animal?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא questions its own reading. Maybe the פסוק is talking about a non-kosher animal given to בדק הבית, not about a blemished animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A non-kosher animal also can never be brought on the altar, so it could fit the wording of the פרשה. If the פסוק meant a non-kosher animal, it would no longer prove anything about blemished altar animals. So the ברייתא has to rule this reading out.

keyTerms.meaning: A non-kosher animal, which can never be an offering
"You say this... or maybe it is only that?": a standard way a ברייתא tests its own reading
Or: introduces the other possible reading

phrases.english: You say it is about blemished animals,
or maybe it is only about a non-kosher animal?

steps.triggerLanguage: אַתָּה אוֹמֵר בְּבַעֲלֵי מוּמִין, אוֹ אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא בִּבְהֵמָה טְמֵאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the ברייתא's reading of the פסוק by offering another possible meaning.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the פסוק is about blemished animals or about a non-kosher animal.

steps.title: A later verse already covers the non-kosher animal
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא begins its answer: a later פסוק already speaks about redeeming a non-kosher animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: When it says "If it is a non-kosher animal, he shall redeem it according to your valuation," a non-kosher animal is already mentioned.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא starts to answer the question. It points to a later פסוק that clearly talks about a non-kosher animal, which sets up the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the non-kosher animal has its own פסוק, the earlier פסוק should not be read as repeating the same case. That pushes the earlier פסוק to mean blemished animals. The ברייתא's conclusion continues on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: When it (the Torah) says: brings another פסוק into the argument
He shall redeem it according to your valuation
This case is already stated

steps.confusionAlert: The answer does not end here. The comma at the end shows the ברייתא is still building its point, and the conclusion comes next.

phrases.english: When it says
"If it is of a non-kosher animal, he shall redeem it according to your valuation"
then a non-kosher animal is already stated,

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּשֶׁהוּא אוֹמֵר ״אִם בִּבְהֵמָה טְמֵאָה וּפָדָה בְעֶרְכֶּךָ״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the question of step 22 by showing that the non-kosher case has its own פסוק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A separate later פסוק already deals with a non-kosher animal, so the earlier פסוק must have a different subject. The full conclusion follows in the next lines.
